paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: A rat or pigeon might not be the obvious choice to tend to someone who is sick, but these creatures have some 26 skills that could help the treatment of human diseases.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老鼠或鸽子可能不是照顾病人的最佳选择，但这些生物拥有一些卓越的技能，可以帮助治疗人类疾病。

paragraphs.sourceText: Pigeons are often seen as dirty birds and an urban 27 , but they are just the latest in a long line of animals that have been found to have abilities to help humans. Despite having a brain no bigger than the 28 of your index finger, pigeons have a very impressive 29 memory. Recently it was shown that they could be trained to be as accurate as humans at detecting breast cancer in images.
paragraphs.translationZh: 鸽子通常被视为肮脏的鸟类和城市公害，但它们只是被发现有能力帮助人类的众多动物中最新的一种。尽管鸽子的大脑不及食指尖那么大，但它们却拥有非常令人印象深刻的视觉记忆。最近的研究表明，经过训练，它们可以像人类一样准确地检测图像中的乳腺癌。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rats are often 30 with spreading disease rather than 31 it, but this long-tailed animal is highly 32 . Inside a rat's nose are up to 1,000 different types of olfactory receptors (嗅觉感受器), whereas humans only have 100 to 200 types. This gives rats the ability to detect 33 smells. As a result, some rats are being put to work to detect TB(肺结核). When the rats detect the smell, they stop and rub their legs to 34 a sample is infected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老鼠通常与传播疾病而不是预防疾病有关，但这种长尾动物非常敏感。老鼠的鼻子内有多达 1000 种不同类型的嗅觉感受器（嗅觉感受器），而人类只有 100 到 200 种。这使老鼠能够察觉轻微的气味。结果，一些老鼠被用来检测结核病。当老鼠闻到气味时，它们会停下来并摩擦腿，表明样本已被感染。

paragraphs.sourceText: Traditionally, a hundred samples would take lab technicians more than two days to 35 , but for a rat it takes less than 20 minutes. This rat detection method doesn't rely on specialist equipment. It is also more accurate — the rats are able to find more TB infections and, therefore, save more lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 传统上，实验室技术人员需要花费两天以上的时间来检查 100 个样本，但对于一只老鼠来说，只需不到 20 分钟。这种老鼠检测方法不依赖专业设备。它也更准确——老鼠能够发现更多的结核感染，从而挽救更多的生命。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Do In-Class Exams Make Students Study Harder?
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2. 课堂考试会让学生更加努力地学习吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: Research suggests they may study more broadly for the unexpected rather than search for answers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究表明，他们可能会更广泛地研究意外情况，而不是寻找答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: A. I have always been a poor test-taker. So it may seem rather strange that I have returned to college to finish the degree I left undone some four decades ago. I am making my way through Columbia University, surrounded by students who quickly supply the verbal answer while I am still processing the question.
paragraphs.translationZh: A. 我一直是一个糟糕的应试者。因此，我回到大学完成大约四十年前未完成的学位似乎相当奇怪。我正穿过哥伦比亚大学，周围都是学生，他们在我仍在处理问题时迅速提供了口头答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Since there is no way for me to avoid exams, I am currently questioning what kind are the most taxing and ultimately beneficial. I have already sweated through numerous in-class midterms and finals, and now I have a professor who issues take-home ones. I was excited when I learned this, figuring I had a full week to do the research, read the texts, and write it all up. In fact, I was still rewriting my midterm the morning it was due. To say I had lost the thread is putting it mildly.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 由于我无法避免考试，所以我目前正在思考什么是最费力且最终有益的。我已经在课堂上度过了无数次期中考试和期末考试，现在我有一位教授可以带回家。当我得知这一点时，我很兴奋，因为我有整整一周的时间来进行研究、阅读文本并将其全部写下来。事实上，期中考试到期的那天早上我仍在重写我的期中考试。说我失去了线索是温和的。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. As I was suffering through my week of anxiety, overthinking the material and guessing my grasp of it, I did some of my own polling among students and professors. David Eisenbach, who teaches a popular class on U.S. presidents at Columbia, prefers the in-class variety. He believes students ultimately learn more and encourages them to form study groups. “That way they socialize over history outside the class, which wouldn’t happen without the pressure of an in-class exam,” he explained, “Furthermore, in-class exams force students to learn how to perform under pressure, and essential work skill.”
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 当我经历了一周的焦虑、过度思考材料并猜测我对它的理解时，我在学生和教授中做了一些自己的民意调查。大卫·艾森巴赫 (David Eisenbach) 在哥伦比亚大学教授有关美国总统的热门课程，他更喜欢课堂上的多样性。他相信学生最终会学到更多，并鼓励他们组建学习小组。 “通过这种方式，他们可以在课堂外就历史进行社交活动，如果没有课堂考试的压力，这是不可能发生的，”他解释说，“此外，课堂考试迫使学生学习如何在压力下表现以及基本的工作技能。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D. He also says there is less chance of cheating with the in-class variety. In 2012, 125 students at Harvard were caught up in a scandal when it was discovered they had cheated on a take-home exam for a class entitled “Introduction To Congress.” Some colleges have what they call an “honor code,” though if you are smart enough to get into these schools, you are either smart enough to get around any codes or hopefully, too ethical to consider doing so. As I sat blocked and clueless for two solid days, I momentarily wondered if I couldn’t just call an expert on the subject matter which I was tackling, or someone who took the class previously, to get me going.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 他还表示，课堂上的各种作弊行为的可能性较小。 2012年，哈佛大学的125名学生被发现在“国会概论”课程的带回家考试中作弊，从而卷入丑闻。有些大学有他们所谓的“荣誉准则”，但如果你足够聪明，能够进入这些学校，那么你要么足够聪明，可以绕过任何准则，要么希望太道德而不会考虑这样做。当我一头雾水地坐了整整两天时，我突然想知道我是否可以打电话给我正在处理的主题的专家，或者以前参加过这门课的人来帮助我继续前进。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Following the Harvard scandal, Mary Miller, the former dean of students at Yale, made an impassioned appeal to her school’s professors to refrain from take-hone exams. “Students risk health and well being, as well as performance in other end-of-term work, when faculty offers take-home exams without clear, time-limited boundaries,” she told me. “Research now shows that regular quizzes, short essays, and other assignments over the course of a term better enhance learning and retention.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 哈佛丑闻发生后，耶鲁大学前学生主任玛丽·米勒 (Mary Miller) 慷慨激昂地呼吁学校的教授不要参加考试。她告诉我：“当教师在没有明确、时间限制的情况下提供带回家的考试时，学生的健康和福祉以及其他期末工作的表现都会受到威胁。” “研究现在表明，在一个学期中定期进行测验、短文和其他作业可以更好地增强学习和记忆力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Most college professors agree the kind of exam they choose largely depends on the subject. A quantitative-based one, for example, is unlikely to be sent home, where one could ask their older brothers and sisters to help. Vocational-type classes, such as computer science or journalism, on the other hand, are often more research-oriented and lend themselves to take-home testing. Chris Koch, who teaches “History of Broadcast Journalism” at Montgomery Community College in Rockville, Maryland, points out that reporting is about investigation rather than the memorization of minute details. “In my field, it’s not what you know—it’s what you know how to find out,” says Koch. “There is way too much information, and more coming all the time, for anyone to remember. I want my students to search out the answers to questions by using all the resources available to them.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 大多数大学教授都同意他们选择的考试类型很大程度上取决于科目。例如，基于定量的人不太可能被送回家，在那里可以请他们的哥哥姐姐帮忙。另一方面，职业类课程，例如计算机科学或新闻学，通常更加以研究为导向，适合带回家进行测试。克里斯·科赫（Chris Koch）在马里兰州罗克维尔的蒙哥马利社区学院教授“广播新闻史”，他指出，报道是为了调查，而不是记住微小的细节。 “在我的领域，重要的不是你知道什么，而是你知道如何找到答案，”科赫说。 “对于任何人来说，信息太多了，而且不断有更多的信息出现。我希望我的学生利用所有可用的资源来寻找问题的答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Students’ test-form preferences vary, too, often depending on the subject and course difficulty. “I prefer take-home essays because it is then really about the writing, so you have time to edit and do more research,” says Elizabeth Dresser, a junior at Barnard. Then there is the stress factor. Francesca Haass, a senior at Middlebury, says, “I find the in-class ones are more stressful in the short term, but there is immediate relief as you swallow information like mad, and then you get to forget it all. Take-homes require thoughtful engagement which can lead to longer term stress as there is never a moment when the time is up.” Meanwhile, Olivia Rubin, a sophomore at Emory, says she hardly even considers take-homes true exams. “If you understand the material and have the ability to articulate (说出) your thoughts, they should be a breeze.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 学生对考试形式的偏好也各不相同，通常取决于科目和课程难度。 “我更喜欢带回家的论文，因为它实际上是关于写作的，所以你有时间编辑和做更多的研究，”巴纳德学院大三学生伊丽莎白·德莱瑟说。然后是压力因素。米德尔伯里学院的大四学生弗朗西斯卡·哈斯 (Francesca Haass) 说：“我发现课堂上的压力在短期内更大，但当你疯狂地吞咽信息时，你会立即得到缓解，然后你就会忘记这一切。收获需要深思熟虑的参与，这可能会导致长期压力，因为永远不会有时间到的时候。”与此同时，埃默里大学二年级学生奥利维亚·鲁宾 (Olivia Rubin) 表示，她几乎不考虑带回家参加真正的考试。 “如果你理解这些材料并且有能力表达你的想法，那么它们应该是轻而易举的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H. How students ultimately handle stress may depend on their personal test-taking abilities. There are people who always wait until the last minute, and make it much harder than it needs to be. And then there those who, not knowing what questions are coming at them, and having no resources to refer to, can freeze. And then there are we rare folks who fit both those descriptions.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 学生最终如何应对压力可能取决于他们个人的应试能力。有些人总是等到最后一刻，让事情变得比需要的更加困难。然后，那些不知道自己会遇到什么问题，也没有资源可以参考的人可能会冻结。然后，我们很少有人同时符合这两种描述。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Yes, my advanced age must factor into the equation (等式), in part because of my inability to access the information as quickly. As another returning student at Columbia, Kate Marber, told me, “We are learning not only all this information, but essentially how to learn again. Our fellow students have just come out of high school. A lot has changed since we were last in school.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 是的，我的高龄必须考虑到等式（等式），部分原因是我无法尽快获取信息。正如哥伦比亚大学的另一位回国学生凯特·马伯 (Kate Marber) 告诉我的那样，“我们不仅学习所有这些信息，而且本质上还学习如何再次学习。我们的同学刚从高中毕业。自从我们上次上学以来，发生了很多变化。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. If nothing else, the situation has given my college son and me something to share, When I asked his opinion on this matter, he responded, “I like in-class exams because the time is already reserved, as opposed to using my free time at home to work on a test,” he responded. It seems to me that a compromise would be receiving the exam questions a day or two in advance, and then doing the actual test in class the ticking clock overhead.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 如果不出意外的话，这种情况给了我和我上大学的儿子一些可以分享的东西，当我询问他对此事的看法时，他回答说，“我喜欢课堂考试，因为时间已经被预留了，而不是利用我在家的空闲时间来做测试，”他回答道。在我看来，一个折衷的办法是提前一两天收到考试问题，然后在课堂上进行实际测试。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Better yet, how about what one Hunter College professor reportedly did recently for her final exam: She encouraged the class not to stress or even study, promising that, “It is going to be apiece of cake.” When the students came in, sharpened pencils in hand, there was not a bluebook in sight. Rather, they saw a large chocolate cake and they each were given a slice.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 更好的是，据报道亨特学院的一位教授最近在期末考试中做了什么：她鼓励全班不要有压力，甚至不要学习，并承诺“这将是小菜一碟”。当学生们手里拿着削好的铅笔进来时，眼前没有一本蓝皮书。相反，他们看到了一个大巧克力蛋糕，并且每人都得到了一块。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Elderly students find it hard to keep up with the rapid changes in education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 老年学生发现很难跟上教育的快速变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Some believe take-home exams may affect students' performance in other courses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 有些人认为带回家的考试可能会影响学生在其他课程中的表现。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Certain professors believe in-class exams are ultimately more helpful to students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 某些教授认为课堂考试最终对学生更有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. In-class exams are believed to discourage cheating in exams.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 课堂考试被认为可以防止考试作弊。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The author was happy to learn she could do some exams at home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 提交人很高兴得知她可以在家做一些考试。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Students who put off their work until the last moment often find the exams more difficult than they actually are.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 把作业拖到最后一刻的学生常常发现考试比实际更难。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Different students may prefer different types of exams.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 不同的学生可能喜欢不同类型的考试。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Most professors agree whether to give an in-class or a take-home exam depends on type of course being taught.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 大多数教授都同意是否进行课堂考试或带回家考试取决于所教授课程的类型。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The author dropped out of college some forty years ago.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 提交人大约四十年前从大学退学。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some students think take-home exams will eat up their free time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一些学生认为带回家的考试会占用他们的空闲时间。

For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 and 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 46 和 50 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: That people often experience trouble sleeping in a different bed in unfamiliar surroundings is a phenomenon known as the “first-night” effect. If a person stays in the same room the following night they tend to sleep more soundly. Yuka Sasaki and her colleagues at Brown University set out to investigate the origins of this effect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们经常在陌生的环境中睡在不同的床上，这种现象被称为“初夜效应”。如果一个人第二天晚上呆在同一个房间里，他们往往会睡得更香。佐佐木由香（Yuka Sasaki）和她在布朗大学的同事着手调查这种效应的起源。

paragraphs.sourceText: Dr. Sasaki knew the first-night effect probably has something to do with how humans evolved. The puzzle was what benefit would be gained from it when performance might be affected the following day. She also knew from previous work conducted on birds and dolphins that these animals put half of their brains to sleep at a time so that they can rest while remaining alert enough to avoid predators (捕食者). This led her to wonder if people might be doing the same thing. To take a closer look, her team studied 35 healthy people as they slept in the unfamiliar environment of the university’s Department of Psychological Sciences. The participants each slept in the department for two nights and were carefully monitored with techniques that looked at the activity of their brains. Dr. Sasaki found, as expected, the participants slept less well on their first night than they did on their second, taking more than twice as long to fall asleep and sleeping less overall. During deep sleep, the participants’ brains behaved in a similar manner seen in birds and dolphins. On the first night only, the left hemispheres (半球) of their brains did not sleep nearly as deeply as their right hemispheres did.
paragraphs.translationZh: 佐佐木博士知道初夜效应可能与人类的进化方式有关。难题在于，当第二天的性能可能受到影响时，会从中获得什么好处。她还从之前对鸟类和海豚进行的研究中了解到，这些动物每次会让一半的大脑进入睡眠状态，这样它们就可以休息，同时保持足够的警觉以避免捕食者。这让她怀疑人们是否也会做同样的事情。为了更仔细地观察，她的团队研究了 35 名健康人，他们在大学心理科学系陌生的环境中睡觉。参与者每人在该部门睡了两个晚上，并通过观察他们大脑活动的技术对其进行仔细监控。佐佐木博士发现，正如预期的那样，参与者第一晚的睡眠质量不如第二晚，入睡时间是第二晚的两倍多，而且总体睡眠时间也更少。在深度睡眠期间，参与者的大脑表现与鸟类和海豚相似。仅在第一天晚上，他们大脑的左半球的睡眠深度就没有右半球那么深。

paragraphs.sourceText: Curious if the left hemispheres were indeed remaining awake to process information detected in the surrounding environment, Dr. Sasaki re-ran the experiment while presenting the sleeping participants with a mix of regularly timed beeps (蜂鸣声) of the same tone and irregular beeps of a different tone during the night. She worked out that, if the left hemisphere was staying alert to keep guard in a strange environment, then it would react to the irregular beeps by stirring people from sleep and would ignore the regularly timed ones. This is precisely what she found.
paragraphs.translationZh: 佐佐木博士很好奇左半球是否确实保持清醒状态来处理周围环境中检测到的信息，因此重新进行了实验，同时向熟睡的参与者提供相同音调的定期蜂鸣声和不同音调的不规则蜂鸣声。她发现，如果左半球在陌生的环境中保持警觉以保持警惕，那么它就会对不规则的蜂鸣声做出反应，将人们从睡梦中惊醒，而忽略定期发出的蜂鸣声。这正是她所发现的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s time to reevaluate how women handle conflict at work. Being overworked or over-committed at home and on the job will not get you where you want to be in life. It will only slow you down and hinder your career goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 是时候重新评估女性如何处理工作中的冲突了。在家庭和工作中过度劳累或过度投入不会让你达到你想要的生活目标。它只会减慢你的速度并阻碍你的职业目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: Did you know women are more likely than men to feel exhausted? Nearly twice as many women than men ages 18-44 reported feeling “very tired” or “exhausted”, according to a recent study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您知道女性比男性更容易感到疲惫吗？最近的一项研究显示，18-44 岁之间感到“非常疲倦”或“精疲力尽”的女性人数几乎是男性的两倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: This may not be surprising given that this is the age range when women have children. It's also the age range when many women are trying to balance careers and home. One reason women may feel exhausted is that they have a hard time saying "no." Women want to be able to do it all volunteer for school parties or cook delicious meals-and so their answer to any request is often “Yes, I can.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 考虑到这是女性生育孩子的年龄范围，这可能并不奇怪。这也是许多女性试图平衡事业和家庭的年龄段。女性可能感到疲惫的原因之一是她们很难说“不”。女性希望能够做学校聚会的志愿者或烹饪美味的饭菜，因此她们对任何请求的回答通常是“是的，我可以”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Women struggle to say “no” in the workplace for similar reasons, including the desire to be liked by their colleagues. Unfortunately, this inability to say "no" may be hurting women's heath as well as their career.
paragraphs.translationZh: 出于类似的原因，女性在工作场所很难说“不”，包括渴望得到同事的喜欢。不幸的是，这种无法说“不”的态度可能会损害女性的健康和职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the workplace, men use conflict as a way to position themselves, while women often avoid conflict or strive to be the peacemaker, because they don't want to be viewed as aggressive or disruptive at work. For example, there’s a problem that needs to be addressed immediately, resulting in a dispute over should be the one to fix it. Men are more likely to face that dispute from the perspective of what benefits them most, whereas women may approach the same dispute from the perspective of what's the easiest and quickest way to resolve the problem-even if that means doing the boring work themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在工作场所，男性利用冲突来定位自己，而女性则经常避免冲突或努力成为和平缔造者，因为她们不想在工作中被视为具有攻击性或破坏性。例如，有一个问题需要立即解决，导致争论是否应该解决。男性更有可能从对自己最有利的角度来面对争议，而女性可能会从解决问题的最简单、最快的方法的角度来处理同样的争议——即使这意味着自己要做一些无聊的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: This difference in handling conflict could be the deciding factor on who gets promoted to a leadership position and who does not. Leaders have to be able to delegate and manage resources wisely – including staff expertise. Shouldering more of the workload may not earn you that promotion. Instead, it may highlight your inability to delegate effectively.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种处理冲突的差异可能是决定谁能晋升到领导职位、谁不能晋升的决定性因素。领导者必须能够明智地委派和管理资源——包括员工的专业知识。承担更多的工作量可能不会让你获得晋升。相反，它可能会凸显出你无法有效地授权。

You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2. 泰山位于山东省西部。海拔1500 余米,方圆约400 平方公里。泰山不仅雄伟壮观,而且是一座历史文化名山,过去 3000 多年一直是人们前往朝拜的地方。据记载,共有72 位帝王曾来此游览。许多作家到泰山获取灵感,写诗作文,艺术家也来此绘画。山上因此留下了许许多多的文物古迹。泰山如今已成为中国一处主要的旅游景点。
